items.title: Delegations
Randy Vaine, resident appeared before Council in support of regulating
notes: Short Term Rentals in Centre Wellington. He indicated the lack of hotels and affordable accommodations in the community support the need for short term rentals. He supported licensing short term rentals provided there are tools available to address noise, litter and garbage, and parking concerns.

items.title: Darcy Saunders, resident shared his experience living adjacent to a
notes: short term rental in Centre Wellington. He explained incidents of drunken disorderly behaviour, noise at all hours, parking issues, invasion of privacy, etc.

items.title: Rohan Sovig, Malone Given Parsons Ltd addressed Council regarding
notes: the Greenfield Density and Intensification Target Preferred Scenario. He noted Malone Given Parsons Ltd., is the planning consultant for Elora Sands Development, the owner of the property at 7581 Sideroad 15, Nichol in Centre Wellington. He indicated they continue to be pleased with the direction the Township, the County and Watson & Associates took with the Lands Needs Assessment (LNA), however, they believe the Township should still rely on the original analysis conducted by Waston & Associates as part of the County LNA. R. Sovig suggested they are concerned the higher intensification rates and density targets outlined in the preferred scenario appear to be unrealistic and unachievable.

items.title: Rob Stovel, RSR Inc. appeared before Council to speak to the
notes: Greenfield Density and Intensification Target Preferred Scenario. He explained his ownership of a small local company, who hires local contractors and strives to provide attainable housing. He explained he has an interest in property at 996 Scotland Street in Fergus and requires approximately 12 acres of land to be brought into the urban boundary to provide attainable housing.

items.title: Janet Harrop, Wellington Federation of Agriculture appeared before
notes: Council regarding the Greenfield Density and Intensification Target Preferred Scenario. She provided statistics indicating over the past 20 years Ontario has lost farmland area that is equivalent to eleven times the size of Toronto, or roughly the entire size of the Greater Toronto Area (1,741,286 acres). Since 2000, we have lost 238 acres of farmland a day and over the last five years, this has increased to 319 acres a day.

She suggested at 319 acres of farmland loss per day by 2051 there will be half the farmland in Ontario than there is today. J. Harrop indicated the Federation recognizes the work completed by Centre Wellington and the County of Wellington and is supportive of scenario 4 which preserves the most agricultural land.

items.title: Consideration of Reports
2023 Audited Financial Statements
notes: Report from M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer Presentation from Matthew Betik, KPMG

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer introduced Matthew Betik, KPMG who provided an overview of the audited financial statements. He indicated it is a clean audit with no significant control deficiencies.

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview on the Township’s asset retirement obligations in accordance with the new PS3280 Asset Retirement Obligations (ARO) public sector accounting standard.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the audited financial statements, including the statement of financial position, the statement of operations, statement of changes in net financial assets, statement of cash flows, and the notes to the financial statements.

Staff responded to questions regarding depreciation or amortization expense, reserves for recreation, quarterly reports and provided clarification related to the asset categories and their alignment with the various Township departments.

items.title: Greenfield Density and Intensification Target Preferred Scenario
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
Presentation from Jamie Cook, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd.

B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development introduced Jamie Cook, Watson & Associates Economists Ltd. J. Cook provided an overview of the exercise, indicating the purpose is to prepare a local assessment of land needs that will prioritize the quantity of land required for servicing to the year 2051. He indicated four (4) scenarios have been developed based on density and intensification levels, and the preferred scenario selected by Council will be utilized for local planning, phasing and servicing plans.

He reviewed the various scenarios and provided highlights on Scenario 3, as follows; Increase to Designated Greenfield Area (DGA) Density, No Change to Residential Intensification Rate, 20% intensification rate, 52 people and jobs/ha in DGA Community Area and Land Need of 132 ha for growth to 2051.

Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development indicated staff is supportive of the recommended scenario 3 and believe the scenario remains realistic and achievable while accomplishing the goal of mitigating the need for urban expansion into prime agricultural areas.
The consultant and staff responded to questions regarding consideration given to existing vacant lands and brownfields, review of historical patterns and data, and the possible timing for a review.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment OP01/23 and Zoning By-law Amendment
notes: RZ01/23 - Decision Report (22 Park Road, Elora)
Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the property is a 0.7 hectare site, on the east side of Wellington Rd 7, west side of Park Road, in the Elora Salem Urban Centre. She noted the property is designated “Industrial” in the Official Plan and adjacent to “Highway Commercial” designation to the west and south, with other Industrial lands to the north and east. M. Iglesias noted the owner is seeking an Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment to change the property from Industrial to Highway Commercial to facilitate a commercial redevelopment of the parcel. She indicated the proposal is consistent with the County and Provincial decision to redesignate the land from Employment Land and the redesignation is compatible with the surroundings, is accessible from a major arterial roadway (County Road 7) and services the needs of the travelling public.
